comments.text: These bytes are copied to $1000–$1048 before execution. At $1000 the entry saves X and Y in $FB/$FC, sets the stack pointer to $FF, clears decimal mode, writes $7F to $DC0D and $DD0D, performs the indexed comparison at $1012, and calls $16CB. If saved Y is 2, saved X values 0, 1 and 2 enter at $1037, $103D and $1043 respectively; other values start at $102E. The call sequence falls through the later entries and loops back to $102E.
Copied to $1049–$106F. Calls $117F, $134F, $0400, $13B4 and $14DB, then calls $1924 with X=$00 and Y=$C2. If $19A3 is $FF, calls $19A4. Finally calls $EB26 and $14B2 and returns.

Copied to $1070–$10AD. Calls $117F, $134F, $0403, $1377 and $1538, then calls $1924 with X=$00 and Y=$C2. While successive checks find $19A3=$FF, calls $1928, then $1593 and $1928, then $19A4. Finally calls $EB26 and $14B2 and returns.
Copied to $10AE–$10B6. Calls $117F and $134F, then jumps to $0406.

Copied to $10B7–$1111. Calls $117F, $134F, $0409, $1377 and $1538, then calls $1924 with X=$00 and Y=$C2. If successive checks find $19A3=$FF, calls $1593, $15EE, $1649 and $1593 in turn, each followed by $1928; if the last check still matches, calls $19A4. Finally calls $EB26 and $14B2 and returns.
Copied to $1112–$111A. Calls $117F and $134F, then jumps to $040C.

Copied to $111B–$114E. Calls $11BB, $134F, $040F, $1377 and $1538, then calls $1924 with X=$00 and Y=$C2. If $19A3=$FF, calls $1593 and $1928; if it still equals $FF, calls $19A4. Finally calls $EB26 and $14B2 and returns.
Copied to $114F–$1157. Calls $11BB and $134F, then jumps to $0412.
Copied to $1158–$117E. Calls $11BB, $134F, $0415, $1377 and $1538, then calls $1924 with X=$00 and Y=$C2. If $19A3=$FF, calls $19A4. Finally calls $EB26 and $14B2 and returns.
Copied to $117F–$11A1. Calls $1777; writes $07 to $DD00, $15 to $D018, $00 to $D015, $1B to $D011 and $08 to $D016; calls $1490, enables interrupts and jumps to $11B7.

Copied to $11A2–$11B6. If A is zero, branch to $11B7. Otherwise call $123E with X=$5F and Y=$12 to copy the message at $125F; then call $19A4 and $11F7 repeatedly until the latter returns zero. The setup at $119F jumps directly to $11B7 over these bytes. A 1,220-instruction direct-control-flow closure from $1000 and the installed IRQ entries does not reach this routine; five scoped VICE wait-to-next-load traces also leave it unentered. This is retained code in the captured engine, with forced-call behavior distinguished from normal entry paths.
Copied to $11B7–$11BA. Calls $14B2 and returns.
Copied to $11BB–$11DC. Calls $1777; writes $07 to $DD00, $15 to $D018, $00 to $D015, $1B to $D011 and $08 to $D016; calls $1490 and jumps to $11F3.
The stored byte $12 is copied to $11DD, immediately after the jump at $11DA to $11F3. Execution from $11BB skips it; other entry paths remain open.

Copied to $11DE–$11F2. If A is one, branch to $11F3. Otherwise call $123E with X=$D7 and Y=$12 to copy the message at $12D7; then call $19A4 and $1216 repeatedly until the latter returns one. The setup at $11DA jumps directly to $11F3 over these bytes. A 1,220-instruction direct-control-flow closure from $1000 and the installed IRQ entries does not reach this routine; five scoped VICE wait-to-next-load traces also leave it unentered. This is retained code in the captured engine, with forced-call behavior distinguished from normal entry paths.
Copied to $11F3–$11F6. Calls $14B2 and returns.

Copied to $11F7–$1215. Calls KERNAL SETLFS with A=$01, X=$08 and Y=$00; calls SETNAM with length 9 and filename address $1235; calls LOAD with A=$00, X=$00 and Y=$20; then reads $2000 into A and returns. The nine filename bytes at $1235 spell SIDE FLAG.
Copied to $1216–$1234. Makes the same SETLFS, SETNAM and LOAD calls as $11F7, reads $2000 into A and returns.
Nine filename bytes copied to $1235–$123D: SIDE FLAG.

Copied to $123E–$125E. Stores the source pointer from X/Y in $FD/$FE, sets the destination pointer to $05B8, then copies 120 bytes in descending index order. For each byte at least $60 it subtracts $60 before writing.
Copied to $125F–$1286: a 40-byte row containing the text “please turn disk over”, surrounded by spaces.
Copied to $1287–$12AE: a 40-byte row of spaces.
Copied to $12AF–$12D6: a 40-byte row containing “press fire button when ready”, surrounded by spaces.
Copied to $12D7–$12FE: a second copy of the row containing “please turn disk over”.
Copied to $12FF–$1326: a second 40-byte row of spaces.
Copied to $1327–$134E: a second copy of the row containing “press fire button when ready”.

Copied to $134F–$1376. Disable interrupts, write $34 to $01 to expose the RAM under I/O, and copy $DC00–$DFFF to $0400–$07FF, one byte from each page for every X value. Then write $36 to $01, enable interrupts and return.

Copied to $1377–$13B3. Disable interrupts, write $35 to $01, clear $145E and call sound initializer $E000 with A=$00. Call $145F, clear twenty pages at $4000–$53FF by advancing the store operand, write $7B to $1905/$1906, clear $145D, call $1760, set $145E to one and return.
Copied to $13B4–$13D7. Disable interrupts, write $35 to $01, call the sound initializer at $E000 with A=$00, call $145F, then clear twenty pages at $4000–$53FF by incrementing the store operand.

Copied to $13D8–$142A. For X=$EF down to zero, write X to $0568,X and $0B to $D968,X. Set the eight VIC sprite X positions alternately to $48 and $60, set their Y positions to $7B for sprites 0, 1, 4 and 5 and $90 for 2, 3, 6 and 7, and clear the X-high and expansion registers.

Copied to $142B–$145C. For X=3 down to zero, write $A0+X and $A4+X to the two groups of screen sprite pointers at $07F8 and $07FC, and write colours 1 and 2 to the corresponding VIC sprite colour registers. Set $1905/$1906 to $7B and $145D/$145E to 1, call $1760 and return.
Two zero bytes copied to $145D/$145E. The restored story code uses $145D to gate part of the raster display setup and $145E to gate sound updates; setup routines change both values.

Copied to $145F–$148F. For each X from $00 through $FF, write $BA to $0400,X and $04B8,X; write zero to $05B8,X, $0600,X and $06F8,X; write $0E to $D800,X and $D840,X; write $0B to $D940,X; then write $0E to $DA30,X, $DA00,X and $DAF8,X. Return after X wraps to zero.
Copied to $1490–$14B1. For each X from $00 through $FF, write $20 to the indexed addresses $0400, $0500, $0600 and $06F8, and write 1 to $D800, $D900, $DA00 and $DAF8. Return after X wraps to zero.

Copied to $14B2–$14D3. For each X from $00 through $FF, write $20 to the indexed addresses $0400, $0500, $0600 and $06F8, and write zero to $D800, $D900, $DA00 and $DAF8. Return after X wraps to zero.
Copied to $14D4–$14DA. Read $0E and keep comparing until its value changes, then return.

Copied to $14DB–$1537. Set $1905/$1906 to $7B and wait for $0E to change. Copy twenty pages from $6400–$77FF to $4000–$53FF. For X from $00 through $FF, copy $7800,X to $6000,X, $7900,X to $6100,X and $7980,X to $6180,X; then write the value at $7A80 to $D800,X and $D840,X and $0B to $D940,X. Set $1905=$3B and $1906=$1B and return.

Copied to $1538–$1592. Set $1905/$1906 to $7B and wait for $0E to change. Copy twenty pages from $6400–$77FF to $4000–$53FF. For X from $00 through $FF, copy $7800,X to $6000,X, $7900,X to $6100,X and $7980,X to $6180,X; then write the value at $7A80 to $D800,X, $D900,X and $D958,X. Set $1905=$3B and $1906=$1B and return.

Copied to $1593–$15ED. Set $1905/$1906 to $7B and wait for $0E to change. Copy twenty pages from $7B00–$8EFF to $4000–$53FF. For X from $00 through $FF, copy $8F00,X to $6000,X, $9000,X to $6100,X and $9080,X to $6180,X; then write the value at $9180 to $D800,X, $D900,X and $D958,X. Set $1905=$3B and $1906=$1B and return.

Copied to $15EE–$1648. Set $1905/$1906 to $7B and wait for $0E to change. Copy twenty pages from $9200–$A5FF to $4000–$53FF. For X from $00 through $FF, copy $A600,X to $6000,X, $A700,X to $6100,X and $A780,X to $6180,X; then write the value at $A880 to $D800,X, $D900,X and $D958,X. Set $1905=$3B and $1906=$1B and return.

Copied to $1649–$16A3. Set $1905/$1906 to $7B and wait for $0E to change. Copy twenty pages from $A900–$BCFF to $4000–$53FF. For X from $00 through $FF, copy $BD00,X to $6000,X, $BE00,X to $6100,X and $BE80,X to $6180,X; then write the value at $BF80 to $D800,X, $D900,X and $D958,X. Set $1905=$3B and $1906=$1B and return.

Copied to $16A4–$16A8. Load $A5 into zero-page byte $0D and return. How this entry is reached remains open. A 1,220-instruction direct-control-flow closure from $1000 and the installed IRQ entries does not reach this routine; five scoped VICE wait-to-next-load traces also leave it unentered. This is retained code in the captured engine, with forced-call behavior distinguished from normal entry paths.

Copied to $16A9–$16CA. Test bits 1 and 6 of $0D, set carry to their exclusive OR, and rotate $0D left through carry. Return with A=$40 and carry equal to the old bit 7. How this entry is reached remains open.
Copied to $16CB–$16F1. Disable interrupts, write $35 to $01, write $1015 to the NMI and reset vectors at $FFFA–$FFFD, clear $145E, and call $17AB. Clear $D020/$D021, enable interrupts and return.

Copied to $16F2–$1723. Read bit $10 of $DC00 and return $80 if it is clear. Otherwise try 30 values from $1724 at $DC00 and compare each $DC01 read with the corresponding byte at $1742. On a match wait until that comparison changes and return the table index; if none match, return $FF.
Copied to $1724–$1741. Thirty values written to $DC00 by the keyboard scan at $16F2.
Copied to $1742–$175F. Thirty values compared against $DC01 by the keyboard scan at $16F2.
Copied to $1760–$1776. Disable interrupts and call $1907 with X/Y=$D7/$17 and A=$20. Write the returned 1 to $D01A, clear bit 7 of $D011, enable interrupts and return.

Copied to $1777–$17A0. Disable interrupts, write $36 to $01, install $17A1 in the KERNAL IRQ vector at $0314/$0315, set raster compare to $20, acknowledge and enable the raster interrupt, clear bit 7 of $D011, and write zero to CIA1 register $DC0E.
Copied to $17A1–$17AA. Increment $0E, write 1 to $D019 and jump to $EA31.
Copied to $17AB–$17C5. Disable interrupts, call $1907 with X/Y=$C6/$17 and A=$20, write the returned 1 to $D01A, clear bit 7 of $D011, and write zero to $DC0E.
Copied to $17C6–$17D6. Call $1916 to save A/X/Y, increment $0E, call $1907 to schedule $17C6 at raster $20, and jump to $191D to restore registers and return from interrupt.

Copied to $17D7–$1804. Save registers through $1916; write zero to $D020/$D021, $06 to $DD00, $80 to $D018, $D8 to $D016 and the value at $1905 to $D011. Increment $0E, schedule $1805 at raster $7A through $1907, and jump to $191D.

Copied to $1805–$1857. Save registers and clear $D020/$D021. If $145D is nonzero, write $0B then the value at $1906 to $D011, write $07/$19/$18 to $DD00/$D018/$D016, set $D022/$D023 to $06/$0E, enable all sprites and clear $D01C. Clear $D020/$D021 again, schedule $1858 at raster $AA and jump to $191D.
Copied to $1858–$188B. Save registers, execute the delay NOPs, write $18 then $78 to $D011, $07 to $DD00, $1D to $D018 and $08 to $D016. Schedule $188C at raster $B0 through $1907 and jump to $191D.
Copied to $188C–$18B3. Save registers, write $78 OR $1903 to $D011, then schedule $18B4 at raster $B8 when $1903 is nonzero, or $18DC at raster $B7 otherwise. Jump to $191D.
Copied to $18B4–$18DB. Save registers, execute the delay NOPs, write $10 OR $1903 to $D011, and call sound update $E13A if $145E is nonzero. Schedule $17D7 at raster $20 and jump to $191D.

Copied to $18DC–$1902. Save registers, execute the delay NOPs and X countdown, write $10 OR $1903 to $D011, and call sound update $E13A if $145E is nonzero. Schedule $17D7 at raster $20 and jump to $191D.

Four initial bytes copied to $1903–$1906: $00, $00, $7B and $7B. The restored story code changes $1903 while scrolling, toggles $1904 to choose a text buffer, and uses $1905/$1906 in raster display writes.
Copied to $1907–$1915. Write X/Y to $FFFE/$FFFF, A to $D012, and 1 to $D019, then return with A=1.
Copied to $1916–$191C. Store A, X and Y in zero-page bytes $02, $03 and $04, then return.
Copied to $191D–$1923. Restore A, X and Y from $02, $03 and $04, then return from interrupt.
Copied to $1924–$1927. Store X/Y in the text pointer at $0F/$10 and fall through to $1928.

Copied to $1928–$19A2. Set $1904 to 1 and clear the two 40-byte buffers at $1A67/$1A8F. Repeatedly wait for $0E to change and call $16F2, storing its result at $19A3. If it is not $FF, advance the text pointer by one and return. Otherwise wait twice more, decrement $1903 modulo eight, and when it becomes seven toggle $1904. On the zero phase, if the byte at the text pointer is zero, shift the screen through $19B9, advance the pointer by one and return; otherwise call $1A12 on that pointer and advance it by $28. Each continuing pass calls $19B9 and $19F5.
Initial zero copied to $19A3. The restored input wait stores the keyboard scanner result at that address; $FF is the no-key result tested by the story sequence.
Copied to $19A4–$19B8. Wait for $0E to change, read $DC00 bit $10 and return if it is clear. Otherwise call $16F2, store its result at $19A3 and repeat while it is $FF.
Copied to $19B9–$19F4. For each X from $27 down to zero, copy nine consecutive 40-byte rows upward: $0680 to $0658, $06A8 to $0680, and so on through $07C0 to $0798. Return after the last column.
Copied to $19F5–$1A11. For each X from $27 down to zero, copy either $1A67,X or $1A8F,X to $07C0,X; select the first when $1904 is zero and the second otherwise.

Copied to $1A12–$1A36. Put X/Y into the load operand at $1A1B/$1A1C. For X from $27 down to zero, read one byte, apply OR $20 and subtract $20 when it is at least $40, then subtract $20 and double it. Store the result at $1A67,X and the result plus one at $1A8F,X.

Twenty-four little-endian addresses from $0400 to $0798, increasing by 40. The copy at $DA37–$DA66 becomes $1A37–$1A66 in the restored story engine. A consumer of the table has not been established. Scoped VICE wait-to-next-load traces from all five title/story/ending captures read none of these bytes; tick-wait and next-load controls fired in every case.
Initial bytes copied to $1A67–$1A8E are 40 spaces. The story routine at $1928 clears this buffer, $1A12 writes converted row bytes to it, and $19F5 can copy it to $07C0–$07E7.
Initial bytes copied to $1A8F–$1AB6 are 40 spaces. The story routine at $1928 clears this buffer, $1A12 writes converted row bytes plus one to it, and $19F5 can copy it to $07C0–$07E7.

A 40-byte row copied to $1AB7–$1ADE contains “this is just some test text!” surrounded by spaces. Whether the game displays this row is open. Scoped VICE wait-to-next-load traces from all five title/story/ending captures read none of these bytes; tick-wait and next-load controls fired in every case.
Zero byte copied to $1ADF immediately after the test-text row.

In a forced call from the copied snapshot, this routine disables interrupts, selects RAM under I/O, and copies through self-modified source and destination operands. The store to $1AF3 resets its source high byte from $DA to $D0; later page starts run from $D1 through $DF while destinations continue through $29. The processor model returns after 26 destination-page passes (26,791 instructions), and VICE reaches the caller with source high $E0 and destination high $2A. It then has selected $01=$35 and enabled interrupts. A normal entry path remains unresolved. A 1,220-instruction direct-control-flow closure from $1000 and the installed IRQ entries does not reach this routine; five scoped VICE wait-to-next-load traces also leave it unentered. This is retained code in the captured engine, with forced-call behavior distinguished from normal entry paths.
115 retained bytes between the self-copy routine and the final 128-byte fragment of the engine page. These bytes remain part of the saved load image; a separate active role is unresolved.

128 retained bytes also present at $2DA0-$2E1F in the Censor introduction and at $FCD7-$FD56 beneath ROM in the title and opening story. They are copied with the complete engine page to $1B80-$1BFF; their original producer and separate consumer remain unresolved. These bytes remain part of the saved load image; a separate active role is unresolved.
Copied to $0400–$0402. Jump to $0418, which selects the filename pattern 1*.
Copied to $0403–$0405. Jump to $0422, which selects the filename pattern 2*.
Copied to $0406–$0408. Jump to $042C, which selects the filename pattern 3*.
Copied to $0409–$040B. Jump to $043D, which selects the filename pattern 4*.
Copied to $040C–$040E. Jump to $0447, which selects the filename pattern 5*.
Copied to $040F–$0411. Jump to $0458, which selects the filename pattern 6*.
Copied to $0412–$0414. Jump to $0462, which selects the filename pattern 7*.
Copied to $0415–$0417. Jump to $0473, which selects the filename pattern 8*.
Copied to $0418–$0421. Set X/Y to $0497 and A to 2, call $047D and return; the two bytes at $0497 are 1*.
Copied to $0422–$042B. Set X/Y to $0499 and A to 2, call $047D and return; the two bytes at $0499 are 2*.
Copied to $042C–$043C. Set X/Y to $049B and A to 2, call $0486 for pattern 3*, write $1B to $D011, then jump to $8009.
Copied to $043D–$0446. Set X/Y to $049D and A to 2, call $047D and return; the two bytes at $049D are 4*.
Copied to $0447–$0457. Set X/Y to $049F and A to 2, call $0486 for pattern 5*, write $1B to $D011, then jump to $8009.
Copied to $0458–$0461. Set X/Y to $04A1 and A to 2, call $047D and return; the two bytes at $04A1 are 6*.
Copied to $0462–$0472. Set X/Y to $04A3 and A to 2, call $0486 for pattern 7*, write $1B to $D011, then jump to $8009.
Copied to $0473–$047C. Set X/Y to $04A5 and A to 2, call $047D and return; the two bytes at $04A5 are 8*.
Copied to $047D–$0485. Store X/Y in $04A7/$04A8 and jump to $04C8.
Copied to $0486–$048E. Store X/Y in $04A7/$04A8 and jump to $04B0.
Eight bytes between loader helpers. These bytes remain part of the saved load image; a separate active role is unresolved.
Copied to $0497–$0498: the two filename bytes 1*.
Copied to $0499–$049A: the two filename bytes 2*.
Copied to $049B–$049C: the two filename bytes 3*.
Copied to $049D–$049E: the two filename bytes 4*.
Copied to $049F–$04A0: the two filename bytes 5*.
Copied to $04A1–$04A2: the two filename bytes 6*.
Copied to $04A3–$04A4: the two filename bytes 7*.
Copied to $04A5–$04A6: the two filename bytes 8*.
Copied to $04A7/$04A8. The entries at $047D and $0486 write this pointer; $04D5/$04D8 read it for SETNAM.
Seven bytes following the loader helper and before the next decoded entry. These bytes remain part of the saved load image; a separate active role is unresolved.
Copied to $04B0–$04C7. Disable interrupts, write $37 to $01, set $0314/$0315 to $EA31, and call $FD15, $FF5E and $E5AD before continuing at $04C8.
Copied to $04C8–$04EA. Write zero to $D020/$D021/$D011, call SETNAM with length 2 and the pointer at $04A7/$04A8, call SETLFS with A/X/Y all 8, call $06A7 with A=1, and return.
Twenty-one bytes after the low-memory loader code and before its next source page. These bytes remain part of the saved load image; a separate active role is unresolved.

Copied to $0500. Initialize X to 2 and use successive bits from $0640 and values from $0612 to select a length. Depending on the bits, the selected value is 1, a two-bit value plus 2 or 5, a three-bit value plus 8, or a ten-bit value. Continue at $053E.

Copied to $053E. Save the selected length at $A8, call $0645, then receive bytes through $067B and store them backwards through ($FC),Y, adjusting the destination high byte and $A9 when the index crosses a page. Continue at $055D.

Copied to $055D. Read bits through $0640; for one branch, read six bits, and for another read nine bits and add $40, carrying into $A7. Store the result in $A6 and set $A8 to 2 before continuing at $0580.

Copied to $0580. Form the source pointer at $F7/$F8 by adding $A6/$A7 to the destination pointer at $FC/$FD and subtracting one. Copy bytes backwards from that pointer to the destination, adjusting high bytes and $A9 across page boundaries. When the requested count is copied, jump to $0502.

Copied to $05B5. Read bits through $0640 and choose a length in $A8 and a distance base and bit count for the continuation at $05C7. The alternatives include lengths 3, 4 or 5, a two-bit value plus 6, or an eight-bit value.

Copied to $0612. Clear $A7, shift bits from $FB into A and $A7 until X bits have been read, and return with X reset to 2. When the bit reservoir empties, fetch another byte through $067B and refill $FB before continuing.

Copied to $0640. Shift the bit reservoir at $FB, returning its next bit in carry when nonzero; on exhaustion branch into the refill path. The entry at $0645 subtracts the length at $A8 from the destination pointer at $FC/$FD, borrowing from its high byte when needed.
Copied to $0651. Set file, device and secondary address to 8, set $B9 to $60, call the KERNAL open routine at $F3D5, then start serial talk and send the secondary address. Continue at $0669.

Copied to $0669. Receive five bytes from the serial channel at $EE13 into $FB-$FF, clear $A9 and $01, and jump to the unpacker at $0500. The offline load map records the headers and consumed file offsets.

Copied to $067B. Select the KERNAL in $01, update two I/O-addressed bytes, and decrement the counter at $FE/$FF. When it reaches the sentinel, branch to $0638, which removes five stack bytes and returns; otherwise receive a serial byte at $EE13, select RAM with $01=0 and return it in A.

Copied to $06A7. Save $01 and the border colour, select the KERNAL and open the file at $0651. While bit 6 of status $90 is clear, call $0669 to decode another segment; then untalk, call $F642, restore the saved border colour and $01, and return.
146 bytes between the decompressor and the 18-byte filename-record loader helpers. These bytes remain part of the saved load image; a separate active role is unresolved.
One retained byte immediately before the filename-record loader entry. These bytes remain part of the saved load image; a separate active role is unresolved.

Copied to $0767. Save X at $02, call SETLFS with file 1, device 8 and secondary address 0, then SETNAM with length 16 and the filename pointer at $FB/$FC. Call KERNAL LOAD with A=0 and X/Y from $0789/$078A, restore X from $02 and return. Its caller remains unestablished. A 1,220-instruction direct-control-flow closure from $1000 and the installed IRQ entries does not reach this routine; five scoped VICE wait-to-next-load traces also leave it unentered. This is retained code in the captured engine, with forced-call behavior distinguished from normal entry paths.
Copied to $0789/$078A. Two-byte destination passed to KERNAL LOAD by $0767; $079B's continuation fills it from offsets 16 and 17 of the record at $FB/$FC.

Copied to $078B. Add 18 to the record pointer at $FB/$FC with carry and jump to $079F to read the record's destination address. A 1,220-instruction direct-control-flow closure from $1000 and the installed IRQ entries does not reach this routine; five scoped VICE wait-to-next-load traces also leave it unentered. This is retained code in the captured engine, with forced-call behavior distinguished from normal entry paths.

Copied to $079B. Store the X/Y record pointer at $FB/$FC, then read bytes 16 and 17 through it into $0789/$078A and return. This uses an 18-byte record with a 16-byte filename followed by a load address. A 1,220-instruction direct-control-flow closure from $1000 and the installed IRQ entries does not reach this routine; five scoped VICE wait-to-next-load traces also leave it unentered.
